newsitem.title: USA: JonBenet ransom note showed hatred for father - report.
newsitem.headline: JonBenet ransom note showed hatred for father - report.

text.p: The ransom note found hours before the body of 6-year-old JonBenet Ramsey was discovered in the basement of her family's home showed hatred for her father, a newspaper reported on Saturday.
The Rocky Mountain News quoted sources who had read the note as saying to John Ramsey: "The two gentlemen who have your daughter don't like you."

The note claims to come from members of a "small foreign faction" and concludes with the signoff "Victory, SBTC," a reference investigators believe to the defunct Subic Bay Training Centre at the U.S. Naval base in the Philippines where John Ramsey was stationed in the late 1960s.
"We respect your business, but not the country it serves," the note said. John Ramsey is president of Access Graphics, a computer reseller based in Boulder, Colorado, where the Ramsey family lives.
The ransom note demanded $118,000 for the safe return of JonBenet, a figure that matched a bonus John Ramsey received from his company in early 1996.
The note also warned the parents not to contact authorities or the child would die.
Boulder officials investigating the murder have not disclosed what the ransom note said, and the newspaper said authorities had no comment on its contents.

The mother, Patricia Ramsey, said she found the ransom note on Dec. 26 as she went downstairs to make her morning coffee. The girl's body was found about eight hours later in a windowless room in the basement.

No arrests have been made and no suspects named. The parents on Wednesday were formally interviewed by the police and a day later spoke to a hand-picked group of local reporters, saying they had nothing to do with their child's murder.
